title: Bundled model pricing / provider-free cost lookup: list catalog providers in sorted order so the chosen entry is stable across filesystems
answers: Model cost shows a different value on macOS vs Linux when no provider is given
Why does the provider-free cost lookup pick a different catalog entry on different machines?
Where is the bundled provider catalog listed for cost lookup?
How do I write a test for 1-hour cache-creation pricing that is not ambiguous across providers?
body:
Path: mlflow/utils/providers.py:_list_provider_names enumerates the bundled provider JSON catalogs (one file per provider, e.g. openai, anthropic, bedrock). Provider-free model cost lookup (calculate_cost_by_model_and_token_usage called without model_provider in tracing) walks these names to find a catalog entry for a model name.
Rule: the names returned by _list_provider_names must be sorted. Directory globs return entries in filesystem-dependent order, so a lookup that takes the first match over an unsorted list can pick a different provider's price on different platforms. The fix was a one-line change: wrap the glob in sorted(...) in _list_provider_names.
Symptom: the same trace with the same model name got a different computed cost on different machines or OSes, because a similarly named model existed in more than one provider catalog and the first-matched catalog differed by filesystem.
Constraints: this makes the order deterministic only; it does not choose a 'correct' provider. Callers that pass model_provider explicitly bypass this search. In tests that check pricing for a model name that exists in several catalogs, pass model_provider explicitly (e.g. model_provider="anthropic") instead of relying on lookup order; tests/utils/test_providers.py asserts the sorted order of provider names.
applies: Applies to provider-free model cost lookup over the bundled catalogs in mlflow/utils/providers.py; does not cover explicit-provider lookups or user-configured pricing.
says: Model cost estimates for the same trace differ between Mac and Linux machines.
Token usage pricing calculations show inconsistent cost totals across different operating systems.
Ensure trace cost calculation produces identical results regardless of host operating system.
Make model token pricing calculations consistent and predictable when no provider is specified.
search: In mlflow/utils/providers.py:_list_provider_names, directory glob results for bundled provider JSON catalogs must be sorted using sorted(...) to prevent platform- and filesystem-dependent catalog ordering. This ensures provider-free cost lookup via calculate_cost_by_model_and_token_usage in tracing yields stable model pricing across machines when a model appears in multiple provider catalogs. The fix establishes deterministic ordering without selecting a preferred provider, does not affect lookups with an explicit model_provider, and is verified in tests/utils/test_providers.py.
